scopeClasses.name: All scopes
scopeClasses.description: The gate does not depend on scopes. Any app for external Zoom users must pass Marketplace review; before that, a beta share link reaches a small number of users.

claims.text: Publishing starts with choosing the audience: users within your own Zoom account, or external Zoom users.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: If you choose to publish your app, select the intended audience.

claims.text: External Zoom users can install the app from the Marketplace only after it passes Zoom's review.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: after it passes Zoom's review process.

claims.text: Apps for users within your own account are for internal use and skip the standard Marketplace review.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: These apps are intended for internal use and don't require the standard Marketplace review.

claims.text: To share the authorization URL with users outside your developer account before review, you select Request to Share.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: To share the authorization URL with users outside of your developer account, select Request to Share.

claims.text: Zoom's app review team answers a beta share request within 3 to 4 business days. This is the beta link, not the full review.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: A member of the Zoom app review team responds to your request no longer than 3-4 business days.

claims.text: A share request needs supporting evidence of your app's security practices.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: Provided supporting evidence of your app's security practices.

claims.text: The Technical Design section must be complete before a share request is approved.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: All required information in the Technical Design section.

claims.text: An approved authorization URL may be shared for 4 weeks.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: Once approved, an authorization URL is permitted to be shared for a standard duration of 4 weeks.

claims.text: A private account level app can be added at most 10 times during sharing.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: The maximum number of additions for a private account-level application is 10.

claims.text: A private user level app can be added at most 100 times during sharing.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: The maximum number of additions for a private user-level application is 100.

claims.text: During beta sharing you may not make any information about the app public.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: Making any information about your app public.

claims.text: You must validate the domains your app's URLs live on before submission.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: Validate your app domains.

claims.text: Reviewers need test credentials that let them use the whole integration.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: provide test credentials that allow Zoom reviewers to fully experience your integration.

claims.text: A test plan goes in the release notes so reviewers can start functional testing.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: include a test plan, so that reviewers have everything they need to begin functional testing

claims.text: A first submission must authorize with the Production client ID.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: Make sure your environment is using the Production Client ID during authorization.

claims.text: Every app goes through functionality, usability and compliance review.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: All apps undergo functionality, usability and compliance review

claims.text: Compliance review happens before security testing.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: Compliance review is done before security testing.

claims.text: Zoom publishes no fixed review duration; it varies with the app's quality, usability and features.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: An app's review time varies based on app quality, usability, quantity and function of features

claims.text: Apps with properly defined scopes get through testing fastest.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: Testing time is typically the shortest for apps that have properly defined scopes

claims.text: A test plan is required for every submission, including resubmissions; missing it is a stated rejection reason.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: A test plan is required for each submission, including re-submissions.

claims.text: Submitting with the wrong client ID is a stated rejection reason.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: It is important that you use the correct client ID when submitting your app for review.

claims.text: Terms of Use, Support, Privacy Policy and Documentation URLs must be on fully qualified domains your company owns.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: must be hosted on fully qualified domain names (FQDNs) owned by your company.

claims.text: Hosting those documents on Google Drive or Dropbox is not permitted.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: Hosting these documents on third-party platforms like Google Drive or Dropbox is not permitted.

claims.text: The app must handle Zoom's deauthorization event notification.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: Handle Zoom's Deauthorization Event Notification

claims.text: Each requested scope needs a justification and detailed testing instructions.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: Developers must provide justification and detailed testing instructions for each requested scope.

claims.text: Creating an app requires being the account owner, an admin, or holding the Zoom for developers role.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: You are either the Zoom account owner, account admin, or have been assigned the Zoom for developers role.

claims.text: Apps are created from the Marketplace's Develop menu, Build an app.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: On the Created apps page, click Develop and select Build an app.

claims.text: After the 4 week beta period you can request two more 4 week extensions.
claims.label: documented
claims.quote: after which you can request two additional 4-week extensions.

claims.text: Zoom staff state a 72 hour SLA for every submission, with the security review taking up to two weeks in the same reply.
claims.label: reported
claims.quote: We have a 72-hour SLA for every submission.

steps.title: Sign in to the Zoom App Marketplace as the account owner, an admin, or a user with the Zoom for developers role
inputs: A Zoom account with one of those roles

steps.title: Create a General app from Develop, Build an app, and set the OAuth redirect URL and scopes
inputs: Redirect URL from your auth config
Scope list with a justification per scope

steps.title: Host Terms of Use, Privacy Policy, Support and Documentation pages on domains your company owns, then validate those domains
steps.detail: Google Drive or Dropbox links are a stated rejection reason.
inputs: Four public URLs on your own domain

steps.title: Implement the deauthorization event handler
inputs: A webhook endpoint for the deauthorization event

steps.title: Complete the Technical Design section and gather evidence of your security practices
steps.detail: Both are checked before a beta share request is approved. A short security document (SDLC, scanning, pen test if any) is what the review team reads.

steps.title: Request to Share for a beta link to users outside your account
steps.detail: Zoom answers within 3 to 4 business days. The link lasts 4 weeks with two 4 week extensions, caps at 10 additions for an account level app or 100 for a user level app, and nothing about the app may be made public meanwhile.
inputs: Completed Technical Design and security evidence

steps.title: Write the test plan and prepare reviewer test credentials
steps.detail: Required on every submission, including resubmissions. Credentials must let reviewers use the whole integration.

steps.title: Submit for Marketplace review using the Production client ID
steps.detail: Zoom publishes no fixed duration. Staff cite a 72 hour SLA per submission with security review up to two weeks; the review covers functionality, usability and compliance, then security.

playbooks.symptom: A customer outside your account gets an error when opening your authorization URL.
playbooks.cause: Apps for external users must pass Marketplace review, and before that the URL can be shared only through an approved beta share request.
playbooks.fix: File a Request to Share with the Technical Design complete and security evidence attached. Expect an answer in 3 to 4 business days and a 4 week window.

playbooks.symptom: The beta link stopped working after a month or after a few installs.
playbooks.cause: Share approvals last 4 weeks and cap at 10 account level or 100 user level additions.
playbooks.fix: Request one of the two 4 week extensions, or submit for the full review if you are at the cap.

playbooks.symptom: The submission was rejected for a missing test plan or the wrong client ID.
playbooks.cause: Both are stated rejection reasons; a test plan is required on every submission and a first submission must use the Production client ID.
playbooks.fix: Add the test plan to the release notes, confirm the client ID, and resubmit.

playbooks.symptom: Rejected over the URLs on the listing.
playbooks.cause: Terms, support, privacy policy and documentation pages must live on domains your company owns; file sharing links are refused.
playbooks.fix: Move the pages to your own domain and validate the domain in the Publish section.
